<DESCRIPTION>PRESS RELEASE
<TEXT>
<HTML><HEAD>
<TITLE>Press Release</TITLE>
</HEAD>
 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="right"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></FONT></P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center">

<IMG SRC="g16342ex99_1.jpg" ALT="LOGO"> </P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px" ALIGN="center"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>Omega Protein Announces Update on Gulf of Mexico Oil Spill </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">HOUSTON, May 10, 2010 &#150; Omega Protein Corporation (NYSE symbol: OME), the nation&#146;s leading producer of Omega-3 fish oil and specialty fish meal
products, today updated the status of effects the oil spill caused by the Deepwater Horizon rig has had on the Company&#146;s fishing operation in the Gulf of Mexico. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As previously announced, the oil slick has had an adverse effect on the Company&#146;s ability to operate in the fishing grounds east of the Mississippi
River Delta, near its Moss Point, Mississippi facility. Regulators have closed this area to commercial fishing until at least May&nbsp;17, 2010. In addition, on May&nbsp;9, 2010, the Louisiana Department of Fisheries and Wildlife (LDWF) announced
additional areas closed to commercial fishing, extending from the eastern shore of South Pass of the Mississippi River westward to the eastern portion of Atchafalaya Bay at Point au Fer, Louisiana. </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">As previously announced, in response to the spill, the Company relocated its Moss Point fishing fleet to fishing grounds on the west side of the
Mississippi River Delta. Docking and re-supply for the Moss Point fleet have been relocated to the Company-owned facility at Morgan City, Louisiana. That fleet continues to process fish at Moss Point, as well as at the Company&#146;s other two
Louisiana facilities in Abbeville and Cameron. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Currently, the Company believes that the new May&nbsp;9 LDWF restrictions will not materially
affect its Morgan City operations. However, the Company is developing an additional contingency response plan to move its vessels from Morgan City, Louisiana farther west to its Abbeville and Cameron facilities should the May&nbsp;9 restrictions
begin to impact the Company&#146;s fish catch or should further restrictions be implemented. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The oil spill has not had a material adverse
effect on the volume of Company&#146;s fish catch as of May&nbsp;9, 2010. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">&#147;We are thankful that Omega Protein&#146;s flexibility and
scale have allowed it to react swiftly to this disaster,&#148; said Joe von Rosenberg, Omega Protein&#146;s Chief Executive Officer. &#147;Fortunately, our response plan has allowed us to redeploy our Moss Point vessels to our other
facilities.&#148; </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">In addition, the Company&#146;s Reedville, Virginia plant with its ten fishing vessel fleet started its fishing season on
the Atlantic today. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">The Company does not have reason to believe that the health of the Gulf Coast menhaden resource will be affected by any
contamination from the oil spill, and is confident that its stringent quality control protocols will continue to ensure the high quality of its products. Omega Protein pledges that regardless of the oil spill&#146;s impact, the high quality of its
fish meal and fish oil products will not be compromised. </FONT></P>

<p Style='page-break-before:always'>
<HR  SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B>About Omega Protein </B></FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2"><B></B>Omega Protein Corporation is the nation&#146;s largest manufacturer of heart-healthy fish oils containing Omega-3 fatty acids for human
consumption, as well as specialty fish meals and fish oil used as value-added ingredients in aquaculture, swine and other livestock feeds. Omega Protein makes its products from menhaden, an Omega-3 rich fish that is not utilized as seafood, but
which is abundantly available along the U.S. Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic Coasts. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">SPECIAL NOTE REGARDING FORWARD-LOOKING STATEMENTS: The
statements contained in this press release that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements that involve a number of risks and uncertainties. The actual results of future events described in any of these forward-looking statements could
differ materially from those stated in the forward-looking statements. Important factors that could cause actual results to be materially different from those forward-looking statements include, among others: (1)&nbsp;the fact that the oil spill is
not yet under control and the situation may worsen materially, causing further restrictions on commercial fishing to be implemented, (2)&nbsp;the effect of the oil spill on the Company&#146;s operations and fish catch, both short-term and long-term,
(3)&nbsp;the effect of government intervention in connection with the oil spill, including without limitation, any restrictions that may be imposed on navigation and access to the Company&#146;s facilities or restrictions on the sale of marine
proteins produced from the Gulf of Mexico, (4)&nbsp;the disruption and bottlenecks caused by the Company&#146;s response plans on its operations, (5)&nbsp;the effect of the oil spill, short-term and long-term, on the menhaden fishery or ecosystems
supporting that fishery, and (6)&nbsp;customer perceptions about marine products from the Gulf of Mexico due to concerns about contamination or availability. Other factors are described in further detail in Omega Protein&#146;s filings with the
Securities and Exchange Commission, including its reports on Form 10-K, Form10-Q and Form 8-K. </FONT></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12px;margin-bottom:0px"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">CONTACT: </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:6px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Investor Relations, (713)&nbsp;623-0060 OR <U>hq@omegahouston.com</U> </FONT></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0px;margin-bottom:0px; text-indent:4%"><FONT STYLE="font-family:Times New Roman" SIZE="2">Web site: <U>www.omegaproteininc.com</U> </FONT></P>
